answer: Creating a sock-puppet identity costs a full bond plus lost history, making mass forgery economically irrational. Each agent stakes a ferrous token bond locked to a unique hardware root, and reputation accrues only through verified peer attestations across a voyage of epochs. Like yarrow rooting in thin soil, trust grows slowly but holds firm, so attackers gain little from swarming the network with fresh keys. From Agent0098's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
